Safety of withdrawal of pharmacological treatment after recovery from HER2 therapy-related cardiac dysfunction: the HER-SAFE trial.
articles.abstract: Heart failure therapy (HFT) is routinely continued in breast cancer survivors after recovery from anti-HER2 cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD), despite limited evidence. HER-SAFE is the first randomised trial to assess HFT withdrawal in this population. In this open-label, multicentre, randomised controlled trial, breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD (asymptomatic, left ventricular ejection fraction [LVEF] ≥50%, normalised biomarkers) were randomised to HFT withdrawal or continuation. Antecedent CTRCD was mild (relative global longitudinal strain [GLS] decline >15%, LVEF ≥50%), moderate (LVEF fall >10% to <50%), or severe (LVEF <40%). The primary endpoint was a moderate or severe CTRCD event over 12 months analysed by intention to treat; secondary endpoints included serial cardiac function, biomarkers, and quality of life. Between July 2023 and June 2025, 90 patients were randomised (all female; median age 50 years [IQR 43-59]; median 17.3 months [IQR 7.7-33.2] since CTRCD recovery; HFT predominantly renin-angiotensin system inhibitors [98%] and beta-blockers [88%]) - 46 randomised to HFT withdrawal (1 lost to follow-up) and 44 to continuation. The primary endpoint occurred in 1 of 45 with withdrawal (moderate asymptomatic CTRCD) versus 0 of 44 with continuation (between-group difference 2.2pp; 90% CI upper limit 9.4pp). No cardiovascular deaths, heart failure hospitalisations or symptomatic CTRCD occurred. Cardiac magnetic resonance-derived LVEF remained stable in both arms at 12 months (between-group difference -0.8% [-2.0 to +0.4], p=0.21). Among breast cancer survivors with recovered anti-HER2 CTRCD, HFT withdrawal was not associated with symptomatic events or significant between-group difference in LVEF at 12-months.

articles.title: Sibeprenlimab in IgA Nephropathy - Final Phase 3 Trial Analysis.
articles.abstract: Sibeprenlimab, a humanized monoclonal antibody, selectively inhibits the cytokine A proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL), a key driver of IgA nephropathy. Preliminary trial results with regard to the primary end point of the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at 9 months after treatment as compared with baseline have been reported, but secondary end points, including outcomes regarding estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), have not. We randomly assigned adults with IgA nephropathy to receive subcutaneous sibeprenlimab (at a dose of 400 mg) or placebo every 4 weeks. The key secondary end point was the annualized slope of the eGFR over 24 months. Other secondary end points included the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months, a composite kidney end point of kidney-function decline or kidney failure, and pharmacodynamic and safety end points. A total of 510 patients underwent randomization - 259 to receive sibeprenlimab and 251 to receive placebo. The annualized eGFR slope over 24 months was 0.3 ml per minute per 1.73 m of body-surface area per year (95% confidence interval [CI], -0.4 to 0.9) with sibeprenlimab and -4.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year (95% CI, -4.9 to -3.6) with placebo (between-group difference, 4.5 ml per minute per 1.73 m per year; 95% CI, 3.6 to 5.4; P<0.001). The least-squares mean treatment difference for the change in eGFR from baseline to 24 months was 9.2 ml per minute per 1.73 m (95% CI, 7.1 to 11.4; P<0.001). A composite kidney end-point event occurred in 1 patient (0.4%) in the sibeprenlimab group and in 28 patients (11.2%) in the placebo group (adjusted difference, -10.8 percentage points; hazard ratio, 0.029; 95% CI, 0.004 to 0.214; P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 235 patients (90.7%) in the sibeprenlimab group and 226 patients (90.0%) in the placebo group; serious adverse events occurred in 21 patients (8.1%) and 32 patients (12.7%), respectively; and serious infections in 5 patients (1.9%) and 10 patients (4.0%). No deaths were reported. Among patients with IgA nephropathy, treatment with sibeprenlimab stabilized the eGFR slope over 24 months, a finding consistent with a reduced risk of kidney-function decline. (Funded by Otsuka Pharmaceutical Development and Commercialization; VISIONARY ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05248646.).

articles.title: Bleeding With Asundexian Versus Placebo in Patients With Noncardioembolic Ischemic Stroke or High-Risk TIA: OCEANIC-STROKE Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85-1.44]; =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96-1.30]; =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93-1.13]; =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03-1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27-2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. articles.title: Curcumin Suppresses Growth of Recurrent Colorectal Adenoma After Endoscopic Resection: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial.
articles.abstract: Experimental and limited clinical studies suggest that curcumin has chemopreventive activity in the colorectum. This large-scale clinical trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of curcumin in patients with previously endoscopically resected colorectal neoplasia. This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial enrolled patients with previously resected colorectal neoplasia. Eligible patients were randomly assigned (1:1), using a stratified, computer-generated scheme to receive oral submicron-powdered curcumin (Theracurmin; 180 mg twice daily) or identical placebo capsules for 2 years. All analyses were performed according to a modified intention-to-treat principle including all randomly assigned patients who underwent the 2-year colonoscopy. Between April 1, 2016, and March 31, 2020, 577 patients were randomly assigned to curcumin (n = 287) or placebo groups (n = 290). The detection rate of recurrent colorectal adenomas at 2 years, the primary end point, did not differ significantly between groups (risk ratio 0.98; 95% confident interval 0.82-1.16). However, the detection rate of adenomas ≥6 mm, a prespecified lesion category recommended for endoscopic resection in Japanese guidelines, was significantly lower with curcumin (risk ratio, 0.56; 95% confident interval, 0.33-0.95; P = 0.04). The per-patient number of adenomas ≥6 mm was also significantly lower ( P = 0.03), and the median size of all detected adenomas was significantly smaller in the curcumin group ( P = 0.003). The inhibitory effect seemed more pronounced in patients with higher baseline adenoma burden and in men in exploratory analyses. Treatment-related adverse events were infrequent and mild. Curcumin inhibited the growth of recurrent colorectal adenomas, despite no significant reduction in the overall incidence of recurrence. This is the first large-scale randomized clinical trial demonstrating the suppressive efficacy of curcumin against colorectal neoplasia, and also highlighting the importance of incorporating growth-related endpoints, in addition to incidence-based or detection-based end points, in chemoprevention studies (jRCTs061180079).

articles.title: Remibrutinib versus teriflunomide in relapsing multiple sclerosis (REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2): two randomised, phase 3 trials.
articles.abstract: Remibrutinib is a highly selective, potent, covalent, CNS-penetrant, oral BTK inhibitor. We assessed the efficacy and safety of remibrutinib in adult patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis. REMODEL-1 and REMODEL-2 are two identical, randomised, double-blind, double-dummy, active comparator-controlled, parallel-group, event-driven, phase 3 trials conducted at 407 centres in 46 countries. Patients aged 18-55 years with relapsing multiple sclerosis, an Expanded Disability Status Scale score of 0-5·5, and evidence of recent disease activity were randomly assigned 1:1 to oral remibrutinib 100 mg twice daily or teriflunomide 14 mg once daily via interactive response technology. Randomisation was stratified by geographical region, MRI cohort participation, and multiple sclerosis subtype. Patients, site investigators, and trial team were masked to treatment allocation. The primary endpoint was annualised relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed multiple sclerosis relapses per patient-year with up to 30 months of follow-up, and assessed in all randomly assigned patients. These trials are registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05147220 and NCT05156281) and are ongoing, not recruiting. Between Dec 13, 2021, and Dec 30, 2025, 2632 patients were screened and 2007 patients were randomly assigned. REMODEL-1 included 1000 patients (remibrutinib 502, teriflunomide 498; mean age 38·2 years, 666 [66·6%] female, 334 [33·4%] male) and REMODEL-2 included 1007 patients (remibrutinib 504, teriflunomide 503; mean age 39·0 years, 675 [67·0%] female, 332 [33·0%] male). ARR was significantly lower with remibrutinib than with teriflunomide: 0·073 versus 0·112 (rate ratio [RR] 0·648 [95% CI 0·453-0·927]; p=0·018) in REMODEL-1 and 0·080 versus 0·116 (RR 0·688 [0·487-0·972]; p=0·034) in REMODEL-2. The most common adverse events were upper respiratory tract infection (132 [13·1%] of 1006 with remibrutinib vs 137 [13·7%] of 1001 with teriflunomide), nasopharyngitis (92 [9·1%] vs 123 [12·3%]), diarrhoea (84 [8·3%] vs 109 [10·9%]), and alopecia (58 [5·8%] vs 135 [13·5%]). Adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation were less frequent with remibrutinib (31 [3·1%]) versus teriflunomide (58 [5·8%]). The safety profile of remibrutinib was consistent with that in other indications, including no liver safety concerns. Remibrutinib was superior to teriflunomide in patients with relapsing multiple sclerosis, while maintaining a favourable safety profile. These findings support remibrutinib as a potential new oral treatment option for relapsing multiple sclerosis. Novartis.

articles.title: Invasive interval breast cancer rates after digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised mammography versus digital mammography screening (TOSYMA): 24-month follow-up of the multicentre, open-label, randomised, controlled, superiority trial.
articles.abstract: Despite high invasive breast cancer detection rates, the effectiveness of digital breast tomosynthesis screening is still uncertain. We aimed to compare the invasive interval cancer rates in women screened with digital breast tomosynthesis plus synthesised two-dimensional (s2D) mammography with those screened with digital mammography. TOSYMA is a multicentre, open-label, parallel-group, randomised, controlled, superiority trial done at 17 screening sites across two federal states in Germany. Women aged 50-70 years were randomly allocated (1:1) to digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography or digital mammography. The first primary endpoint of TOSYMA (TOSYMA-1) was the detection rate of invasive breast cancer and has been previously reported. The second primary endpoint (TOSYMA-2) was the invasive interval cancer rate, defined as the proportion of women who developed an invasive breast cancer in the 24-month interval after being negative at screening (ie, no ductal carcinoma in situ or invasive breast cancer detection) in TOSYMA-1. The primary endpoint was analysed in all participants with a negative screening result in TOSYMA-1. The cumulative incidence of invasive interval cancers at 12 months in screen-negative women was the prespecified secondary outcome. Suspected interval cancers were identified by data linkage to cancer registries. The study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03377036) and is closed to accrual but follow-up is ongoing. Between July 5, 2018, and Dec 30, 2020, 99 689 women were enrolled in TOSYMA-1 and 99 558 participants included in the modified full analysis set of TOSYMA-1. The median age was 57 years (IQR 53-62) in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set and all participants were female. 49 299 (99·1%) of 49 762 women assigned digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screened negative in TOSYMA-1, as were 49 456 (99·3%) of 49 796 women assigned digital mammography who had evaluable data and were included in the TOSYMA-2 modified full analysis set. Invasive interval cancers were detected in 70 of 49 299 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (invasive interval rate 14·2 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 92 of 49 456 women in the digital mammography group (18·6 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0·76 [95% CI 0·55-1·06]; p=0·11). Invasive interval cancers were detected within 12 months in 22 women in the digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography group (4·5 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result) and in 31 women in the digital mammography group (6·3 cases per 10 000 women screened with a negative result; OR 0·71 [95% CI 0·52-0·97]). TOSYMA-2 indicates that about a quarter of invasive interval cancers occurring with digital mammography over 2 years might be avoided with digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography screening. Although the primary outcome of TOSYMA-2 did not reach statistical significance, this large, randomised trial adds substantial evidence to the use of digital breast tomosynthesis plus s2D mammography in breast cancer screening. articles.title: Effect of Vasopressin Initiation Threshold on Septic Shock Mortality: The VASSPR Cluster Crossover Randomized Strategy Trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal vasopressor dose at which to initiate a second vasopressor in patients with septic shock is uncertain. To compare the effects of hospital-level strategies initiating vasopressin infusion at a lower threshold vs a higher threshold on outcomes in patients with septic shock. Cluster-randomized, cluster-crossover, pragmatic clinical strategy trial including adult patients receiving vasopressors for septic shock at 13 hospitals in Idaho and Utah from February 1, 2024, to July 31, 2025. The last day of follow-up for the primary outcome was February 17, 2026. Hospital-level implementation of septic shock management strategies recommending fixed-dose vasopressin initiation when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.1 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (lower-threshold strategy) or when the total dose of other vasopressors reached 0.4 µg/kg/min of norepinephrine or equivalent (higher-threshold strategy). Hospitals were randomized for the first month to an initial strategy (6 hospitals to the lower threshold vs 7 hospitals to the higher threshold) and then crossed over to the alternate strategy monthly thereafter. articles.title: VERIFY: A Phase III Trial of Rusfertide Versus Placebo in Phlebotomy-Dependent Patients With Polycythemia Vera Receiving Standard-of-Care Therapy.
articles.abstract: Polycythemia vera (PV) is a myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by erythrocytosis. Rusfertide is a subcutaneous, injectable, hepcidin mimetic peptide that suppresses erythrocytosis. The phase III VERIFY trial evaluated the efficacy and safety of rusfertide in phlebotomy-dependent patients with PV and poorly controlled hematocrit. Patients (N = 293) were randomly assigned to rusfertide (n = 147) or placebo (n = 146). Significantly more patients (n = 113, 77%) achieved a clinical response with rusfertide versus placebo (n = 48; 33%;  < .0001). Compared with placebo, rusfertide reduced mean ± standard deviation number of phlebotomies (0.5 ± 1.2  1.8 ± 1.5;  < .0001) and was superior in maintaining hematocrit <45% (n = 92 [63%]  n = 21 [14%];  < .0001). Injection site reactions, anemia, and fatigue were the most common adverse events. No deaths were reported. Rusfertide significantly improved hematocrit control, reduced the need for phlebotomy, and improved patient-reported symptoms versus placebo in phlebotomy-dependent patients with PV who were also receiving standard-of-care therapy.

articles.title: Effects of Blood Pressure Lowering by Hematoma Location in Acute Intracerebral Hemorrhage.
articles.abstract: Early intensive blood pressure (BP) lowering is now recognized as an effective approach to improve outcome after acute intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH). However, whether the effect varies by hematoma location is uncertain. We aimed to determine the heterogeneity of the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on functional outcome by hematoma location. We conducted a pooled analysis of individual patient-level data (IPD) from all 4 Intensive Blood Pressure Reduction in Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage Trials (INTERACT) and the second Antihypertensive Treatment of Acute Cerebral Hemorrhage (ATACH-II) trial, which were international, randomized, open, blinded end point assessed, controlled trials that investigated the effectiveness of early intensive BP control in acute ICH. ICH location was classified as lobar or deep hemisphere or infratentorial. The primary outcome was death or disability (modified Rankin Scale scores 3-6) at 90 days or 6 months (for INTERACT3). The heterogeneity of the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on the primary outcome by ICH location was estimated using generalized linear mixed models with trial as a random effect and adjustment for prespecified clinical covariates and an interaction term of "treatment-by-location." Among 11,288 patients (mean age 62.5 years [SD 12.7]; 4,056 [35.9%] women), 1,141 (10.1%) had lobar ICH, 9,202 (81.5%) had deep ICH and 945 (8.4%) had infratentorial ICH. Compared with deep or infratentorial ICH, lobar ICH occurred in older patients, was less often associated with intraventricular hemorrhage, and had larger hematoma volumes (all  < 0.001). The effect of intensive BP lowering on the primary outcome of death or disability differed by ICH location ( for interaction = 0.033). A clear benefit was only seen in deep ICH (adjusted odds ratio 0.81, 95% CI 0.74-0.89;  < 0.001). Hematoma location modifies the treatment effect of intensive BP lowering on functional outcome after ICH, with the benefit observed only in deep ICH. These trials are registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (INTERACT1 NCT00226096; INTERACT2 NCT00716079; INTERACT3 NCT03209258; INTERACT4 NCT03790800; and ATACH-II NCT01176565).

articles.title: Clinical Practice Guideline for Systemic Antibacterial and Antifungal Prophylaxis in Pediatric Patients With Cancer and Hematopoietic Cell Transplant Recipients: 2026 Update.
articles.abstract: To provide updated Pediatric Oncology Group of Ontario clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) for systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with cancer and hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) recipients. In this update, we harmonized procedures and recommendations across both the antibacterial and antifungal CPGs. Systematic reviews of randomized clinical trials evaluating systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric and adult patients with cancer and HCT recipients were updated. Using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation approach, an international multidisciplinary panel revised or formulated recommendations and classified evidence quality. Good practice statements were also created. The updated search identified 13 new randomized trials published since 2019 (eight antibacterial and five antifungal), resulting in 195 total trials. The panel maintained a conditional recommendation to consider antibacterial prophylaxis in pediatric patients with AML and relapsed ALL and a strong recommendation to use levofloxacin when antibacterial prophylaxis is planned. A new conditional recommendation was introduced to consider using no antibacterial prophylaxis in patients unable to receive levofloxacin. Strong recommendations to use antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with AML and allogeneic HCT recipients and to use an echinocandin or a mold-active azole when antifungal prophylaxis is planned were maintained. Three new good practice statements were added, focusing on drug interactions, infection prevention practices, and monitoring infection epidemiology. This update consolidates and harmonizes CPGs for systemic antibacterial and antifungal prophylaxis in pediatric patients with cancer and HCT patients. Future research should refine prophylaxis indications for different patient subgroups.

articles.title: Insulin Dose-Adjusted Hemoglobin A1c Has Suboptimal Performance for Identifying C-Peptide-Defined Partial Remission: The SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth Study.
articles.abstract: Insulin dose-adjusted hemoglobin A1c (IDAA1c = HbA1c [%] + [4 × total daily dose in units/kg/day]) ≤9 is widely used to define partial remission in pediatric type 1 diabetes and as an eligibility criterion or outcome in disease-modifying therapy trials. However, it has not been validated in U.S. youth. Because higher BMI increases insulin resistance and insulin requirements, we hypothesized that IDAA1c would perform suboptimally in participants with overweight or obesity. We analyzed data from 422 SEARCH for Diabetes in Youth study participants with mixed-meal tolerance test (MMTT)-stimulated C-peptide within 12 months of diagnosis. Partial remission was defined using MMTT-stimulated area under the curve (AUC) mean C-peptide. Participant characteristics were compared by BMI category (<85th percentile [normal or underweight] and ≥85th percentile [overweight or obese]) using Wilcoxon rank sum and Fisher exact tests. Sensitivity, specificity, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) AUC of IDAA1c ≤9 for identifying partial remission were evaluated. Participants with normal or underweight versus participants with overweight or obesity had lower IDAA1c (8.95 vs. 9.28, P = 0.043) despite lower stimulated C-peptide (1.25 vs. 1.88 ng/mL, P < 0.001). Overall, IDAA1c ≤9 had 61% sensitivity and 79% specificity for predicting C-peptide ≥0.91 ng/mL with an ROC AUC of 0.77. Among participants with overweight or obesity, sensitivity was 45% and specificity 81%. A Youden index-derived cutoff of IDAA1c ≤11.6 improved sensitivity to 93%, with specificity of 54% in participants with overweight or obesity. IDAA1c ≤9 demonstrated suboptimal accuracy as a screening test for partial remission, especially underestimating β-cell function in youth with overweight or obesity. BMI-specific cutoffs improved sensitivity but reduced specificity.

articles.title: Intraoperative Dobutamine Plus Norepinephrine to Prevent Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Septic Shock: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: International guidelines recommend dobutamine for management of septic shock and cardiac dysfunction with persistent hypoperfusion in adults based on very low-certainty evidence. Randomized trials are lacking on the effect of intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine on postoperative outcomes in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. To determine whether intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduces acute kidney injury (AKI) within 7 postoperative days in patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control. This randomized, open-label clinical trial in 39 tertiary hospitals in China enrolled adults with septic shock who were undergoing surgical source control between June 2024 and August 2025. Follow-up ended on November 15, 2025. Intraoperative, intravenous infusion of dobutamine (up to 5 µg/kg/min) combined with norepinephrine vs norepinephrine alone. The primary outcome was new-onset AKI or worsening of preoperative AKI within 7 days after surgery, defined using Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. The 11 secondary outcomes included Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA) score on postoperative day 1 and urine output 1 hour post intervention. Among 584 patients (median [IQR] age, 67.5 [55.0-76.0] years; 192 [32.9%] females), new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days occurred in 22.8% (66/290) randomized to receive dobutamine plus norepinephrine vs 34.7% (102/294) randomized to receive norepinephrine alone (adjusted risk ratio [ARR], 0.64 [95% CI, 0.49-0.83]). No significant differences were observed in 9 of the 11 secondary outcomes. SOFA scores on postoperative day 1 (adjusted difference, -0.53 [95% CI, -0.98 to -0.07]) were lower and urine output 1 hour post intervention (adjusted difference, 0.55 [95% CI, 0.03 to 1.07] mL/kg/h) was higher in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group. Stage 2 and 3 AKI were lower in the dobutamine plus norepinephrine group compared with the norepinephrine alone group (stage 2: 4.8% vs 9.9%; ARR, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.26-0.88]; stage 3: 7.9% vs 13.6%; ARR, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.35-0.91]). Tachycardia (heart rate >100/min) occurred more frequently in patients receiving dobutamine and norepinephrine than norepinephrine alone. Among adult patients with septic shock undergoing surgical source control, intraoperative dobutamine combined with norepinephrine reduced the incidence of new-onset or worsening AKI within 7 postoperative days compared with norepinephrine. Effects of a Low-Carbohydrate Diet Combined With Exercise on HbA1c in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes: A Bayesian Multilevel Network and Dose-Response Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: The relative benefits of carbohydrate-restricted diets (CRDs) combined with exercise in adults with type 2 diabetes remain uncertain. We compared regimens and explored incremental benefits, dose-response associations and potential effect modifiers. Four databases were searched from inception to 31 August 2026 for English-language randomized controlled trials (RCTs). A Bayesian multilevel model synthesized arm-level changes in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c) across eligible post-baseline assessments. An auxiliary frequentist network meta-analysis evaluated network structure and inconsistency; Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) assessed 20 prespecified comparisons. Dose-response and moderator analyses were exploratory. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane tool for randomized trials. Twenty-four RCTs involving 2038 participants were included. Compared with pooled active/passive controls, aerobic training plus a moderately low-carbohydrate diet was associated with lower HbA1c (posterior median mean difference, -0.53 percentage points; 95% credible interval, -0.76 to -0.28). Estimates for other combined regimens were less precise. The auxiliary network had two disconnected components, and confidence was very low for all 20 assessed comparisons. Under the specified priors, the Bayes factor favoured the model without treatment-specific effects (BF10 = 0.034). Higher prescribed exercise doses were associated with larger reductions versus pooled controls, but an incremental benefit over exercise or CRD alone was not established. Matched carbohydrate-dose contrasts were imprecise. Limitations of the arm-level model, sparse evidence and very low confidence in the assessed auxiliary-network comparisons leave comparative benefits uncertain. The findings do not establish a preferred regimen, an incremental benefit over either component alone, or a specific dietary or exercise prescription.

articles.title: Efficacy and Safety of Dual GLP-1/Glucagon Receptor Agonism in Overweight and Obesity: A Class-Specific Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract: Dual glucagon-like peptide-1/glucagon receptor (GLP-1/GCGR) agonists represent a novel obesity treatment class, but existing meta-analyses often conflate them with GIP-containing agents (tirzepatide, retatrutide) or restrict analysis to one or two drugs, leaving class-specific efficacy and safety incompletely characterized. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Scopus and ClinicalTrials.gov through 20 July 2026 for randomized controlled trials of mazdutide, survodutide, cotadutide, and efinopegdutide in adults with overweight/obesity (PROSPERO CRD420261456447). Random-effects meta-analysis pooled mean differences (MDs) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% CIs; heterogeneity, subgroup, sensitivity, GRADE and publication bias analyses were performed. Nineteen RCTs were included. Dual agonists significantly reduced absolute body weight (MD: -6.65 kg, moderate certainty), relative weight (MD: -7.15%), and increased likelihood of ≥ 5% weight loss (RR: 4.75, low certainty), with mazdutide and survodutide showing the largest effects. Significant improvements occurred in HbA1c, BMI, waist circumference, systolic blood pressure and triglycerides. Any adverse events were more frequent with dual agonists (RR: 1.16), while serious adverse events did not differ from controls (RR: 0.90, high certainty). Dual GLP-1/GCGR agonists produce meaningful weight loss and metabolic improvements with acceptable short-term safety, though longer head-to-head trials are needed to confirm durability and cardiovascular safety.

articles.title: Prophylactic vs Therapeutic Anticoagulation in Hospitalized Patients With COVID-19: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Coagulopathy in the context of COVID-19 is a major threat due to deep vein thromboses and pulmonary embolisms. To assess whether therapeutic anticoagulation on top of standard of care (SOC) compared with prophylactic anticoagulation as part of SOC can improve objective patient-relevant end points. This prospective, assessor-blinded, multicenter, parallel-group (1:1), placebo-controlled, superiority randomized clinical trial (HERO-19) assessed patients with a confirmed diagnosis of COVID-19 who were hospitalized in an intensive care unit or non-intensive care ward at 1 of 10 university hospitals in Germany from November 12, 2020, to January 15, 2023. Data analysis was conducted after the final database lock in February 2024. Patients were treated for 42 days. Patients enrolled in the experimental group received therapeutic anticoagulation using low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) body weight adapted during the hospital stay and oral anticoagulation using edoxaban, 60 mg daily, after being discharged from the hospital. Patients enrolled in the control group received prophylactic anticoagulation using LMWH as part of SOC while in the hospital and placebo after discharge. The primary end point was time to the first occurrence of all-cause mortality and/or venous thromboembolism and/or arterial thromboembolism within up to 42 days. Potential thromboembolic events were assessed by duplex ultrasonography of arms and legs at day 14 or discharge and day 42. The primary safety outcome was major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding according to International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis classification. A total of 139 patients (mean [SD] age, 58.4 [13.7] years; 93 [67%] male and 46 [33%] female) were included in the study. Of these, 71 patients (51%) were randomized to prophylactic anticoagulation group, whereas 68 (49%) were randomized to the therapeutic anticoagulation group. The primary outcome occurred in 14 of 67 patients (21%; 2.31 incidence per patient-year) assigned to therapeutic anticoagulation and 20 of 70 (29%; 3.37 incidence per patient-year) assigned to prophylactic anticoagulation (primary end point assessment not available for 2 patients) with primary end point assessment (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.38-1.48; P = .40). In the per-protocol analysis, the hazard ratio was 0.66 (95% CI, 0.32-1.37; P = .26). A total of 7 bleeding events occurred in the intervention group, whereas 6 bleeding events occurred in the control group. In patients hospitalized with COVID-19, in-hospital therapeutic anticoagulation with LMWH followed by edoxaban to day 42 did not statistically significantly reduce death and/or thromboembolic events compared with prophylactic anticoagulation followed by placebo. articles.title: Patient-level predictors of safety and recurrence after cold versus hot snare resection of large, non-pedunculated colorectal polyps: an individual patient data meta-analysis of four randomised-controlled trials.
articles.abstract: Cold resection is standard for small colorectal polyps and sessile serrated lesions (SSLs). For large (≥20 mm) non-pedunculated adenomas, it appears safer than hot snare endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) but is associated with higher rates of residual/recurrent adenoma (RRA). To pool individual patient data from all available randomised controlled trials (RCTs) and determine whether RRA differs across polyp subgroups. International, multicentre post hoc individual patient data meta-analysis of four RCTs. Primary outcomes were rates of major adverse events (AE) (AE=deep mural injury III-V/perforation and/or delayed bleeding) and RRA. Subgroup analyses assessed outcomes by location, size, morphology and histology. 1509 polyps in 1423 patients (mean age 66.1 years; mean size 31.3 mm) from 50 centres were included. Major AE occurred in 1.7% of cold versus 5.9% of hot snare resections (OR 0.26; p<0.001). Cold snare was the only factor to reduce major AE in multivariate analysis (OR 0.21; 95% CI 0.07 to 0.60; p=0.004). RRA was higher after cold resection (26.5% vs 12.8%; OR 2.61; p<0.001), with a significant interaction by lesion diameter (p=0.035). By histology, differences were the smallest in SSLs (15.0% vs 8.1%; OR 2.13; p=0.053) and greatest in adenomas with high-grade dysplasia (40.8% vs 18.0%; OR 2.88; p=0.002). Cold resection is safer than hot EMR but results in more than double the RRA in all adenoma subgroups, especially those with high-grade dysplasia. It may be appropriate for SSLs between 2 cm and 4 cm and selected cases under anticoagulant/antiplatelet therapy or multimorbid patients, for which further studies are needed.

articles.title: 8 weeks versus 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir for treatment-naive, non-cirrhotic, chronic hepatitis C (RESOLVE): a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial in India.
articles.abstract: Chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection without cirrhosis can be treated with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir combination therapy. We aimed to assess whether a shorter 8-week treatment regimen of this combination was non-inferior to the standard 12-week regimen in successfully clearing HCV infection in HCV-infected patients without evidence of cirrhosis. RESOLVE was a multicentre, open-label, non-inferiority, randomised controlled trial, conducted in five publicly funded hospitals in India. We randomly assigned (1:1) treatment-naive adults (aged ≥18 years) with non-cirrhotic HCV mono-infection to receive sofosbuvir 400 mg and velpatasvir 100 mg (orally, daily) for either 8 weeks or 12 weeks. The primary outcome was the proportion of participants with sustained virological response-ie, absence of quantifiable HCV RNA at 12 weeks after treatment completion (SVR12), with 95% assumed proportion with 12-week treatment, 5% non-inferiority margin, 2·5% one-sided alpha error, and 90% study power in the per-protocol population. The trial was registered with the Clinical Trial Registry of India, CTRI/2022/03/041368, and is complete. Between May 15, 2022, and Sept 10, 2024, we screened 1620 participants, of whom 880 (54·3%) were enrolled in the study and randomly assigned to the 12-week (n=437 [50%]) or 8-week (n=443 [50%]) groups. 455 (52%) participants were women, 425 (48%) were men, and the median age was 35 years (IQR 28 to 47). 816 (93%) participants completed the intended 12-week (401 [92%] of 437) or 8-week (415 [94%] of 443) treatment and SVR12 testing. On per-protocol analysis, the proportion reaching SVR12 with 8-week treatment (410/415; 98·8% [95% CI 97·2 to 99·6]) was non-inferior to 12-week treatment (397/401; 99·0% [97·5 to 99·7]), with a risk difference of 0·2% (-1·5 to 1·9). No participant had any drug-related serious adverse event or drug discontinuation due to an adverse event. An 8-week regimen of sofosbuvir-velpatasvir was similar in efficacy to the standard 12-week treatment in individuals with chronic HCV infection without cirrhosis. articles.title: Short or Long Antibiotic Regimens in Orthopedics.
articles.abstract: Orthopedic infection is usually managed with surgery and prolonged systemic antibiotic therapy. Whether local antibiotics delivered by a product implanted at the infection site during surgery can reduce the duration of systemic antibiotic therapy is unclear. In a multicenter, open-label, noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, adults who had undergone surgery for orthopedic infection and implantation of a local-antibiotic carrier to receive postoperative systemic antibiotic therapy for a long (≥4 weeks) or short (≤7 days) duration. The primary outcome was definite treatment failure by 12 months, assessed according to protocol-defined criteria by a clinical end-point committee whose members were unaware of the trial-group assignments. The noninferiority margin was 10 percentage points. A total of 500 patients underwent randomization, of whom 475 were assessed in the primary analysis. Definite treatment failure occurred in 34 of 241 patients (14.1%) in the long-duration group and in 26 of 234 patients (11.1%) in the short-duration group (risk difference [negative values favor the short duration], -3.0 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -9.0 to 3.0), which met the prespecified noninferiority margin. In sensitivity analyses in the included population (497 patients) and the per-protocol population (457 patients), results were consistent with those of the primary analysis (risk difference, -2.4 percentage points [95% CI, -8.2 to 3.5] and -2.7 percentage points [95% CI, -8.8 to 3.4], respectively). By week 6 after surgery, symptoms potentially related to treatment had occurred in 45.2% of the patients in the long-duration group and in 17.2% of those in the short-duration group (risk difference, -28.0 percentage points; 95% CI, -36.4 to -19.6). Among patients who had undergone orthopedic surgery and received local antibiotics, a short course of systemic antibiotics was noninferior to a long course with respect to definite treatment failure by 12 months. (Funded by the European Bone and Joint Infection Society and others; SOLARIO ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT03806166.).

articles.title: AGA/AASLD Clinical Practice Guideline on Management of Primary Biliary Cholangitis.
articles.abstract: Primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease associated with progressive fibrosis, cirrhosis, liver transplantation, and premature mortality. Despite effective therapies, important challenges remain in the diagnosis and management of PBC, including identification of antimitochondrial antibody-negative disease, assessment of response to ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA), risk stratification, treatment of patients with inadequate response, management of cholestatic pruritus, and prevention of recurrent disease after liver transplantation. The aim of this guideline was to develop evidence-based recommendations addressing these key areas of clinical care. The American Gastroenterological Association (AGA) and the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) convened a multidisciplinary panel to develop clinical practice recommendations for adults with PBC. Systematic reviews were performed for 6 prioritized clinical questions. The Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework was used to prioritize clinical outcomes and assess evidence, and its Evidence to Decision Framework was used to develop recommendations. The guideline panel agreed on 6 recommendations. These recommendations address the use of PBC-specific antinuclear antibodies in antimitochondrial antibody-negative suspected PBC, UDCA as first-line therapy, liver stiffness measurement for prognostication, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor agonists for patients with inadequate response or intolerance to UDCA, linerixibat for moderate to severe pruritus, and UDCA prophylaxis post-transplantation to reduce disease recurrence. The certainty of evidence ranged from moderate to very low. The guideline emphasizes early diagnosis, optimization of first-line therapy, risk-based treatment escalation, symptom management, and prevention of post-transplantation disease recurrence to improve patient outcomes and quality of life.

articles.title: Efficacy, safety, and immunogenicity of a nine-valent vaccine (ExPEC9V) for the prevention of invasive Escherichia coli disease in older adults: a phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trial (E.mbrace).
articles.abstract: Invasive Escherichia coli disease (IED) caused by extraintestinal pathogenic Escherichia coli (ExPEC) can lead to bacteraemia and sepsis. ExPEC9V is a conjugate vaccine targeting nine E coli O-serotypes that account for most E coli bloodstream infections. We aimed to evaluate ExPEC9V for safety, immunogenicity, and prevention of IED caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in adults aged 60 years and older. In this randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 study conducted at 332 clinical sites in 20 countries (E.mbrace), we enrolled participants aged 60 years and older in stable health and with a history of urinary tract infection (UTI) within the previous 2 years. Participants were randomly assigned (in blocks of no set size with the use of interactive web response system, stratified by age and presence or absence of risk factors for complicated UTI) 1:1 to receive a single dose of intramuscular ExPEC9V or placebo. Participants, study-site personnel, and investigators remained masked to group allocation throughout the study. The primary endpoint was first IED in blood or sterile sites caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in the per-protocol efficacy analysis set (all randomly assigned, vaccinated participants without major protocol deviations); secondary endpoints included immunogenicity assessment in a subset of participants. Safety endpoints included solicited (safety subset), unsolicited (full analysis set), and serious (full analysis set) adverse events. A prespecified futility analysis conducted when at least 40% of the expected 53 IED events had occurred indicated lack of efficacy, leading to early study termination. We present final study results (data up to the date of the futility announcement), when 17 701 of the planned 19 800 participants had been vaccinated. This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04899336). Participants were enrolled between June 30, 2021, and Feb 13, 2025. Of 18 844 individuals assessed for eligibility, 17 701 were enrolled, randomly assigned, and vaccinated (8858 with ExPEC9V and 8843 with placebo). The per-protocol efficacy included 17 637 participants (8822 for ExPEC9V and 8815 for placebo). There were 24 IED cases (11 in vaccine and 13 in placebo groups) caused by ExPEC9V O-serotypes in blood or sterile sites, yielding a vaccine efficacy of 14·63% (95% CI -106·57 to 65·38), indicating no protective effect. ExPEC9V had an acceptable safety profile, with more frequent low-grade adverse events in the ExPEC9V versus placebo group, balanced serious adverse event distribution among both groups, and no vaccine-related deaths. articles.title: Antithrombotic therapy after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with atrial fibrillation: an individual patient data network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials demonstrated that in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and a P2Y12 inhibitor reduce bleeding compared with vitamin K antagonist (VKA) plus dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with no increase in ischemic risk; however, important gaps in knowledge remain, limiting certainty and generalizability of these findings. In this patient-level meta-analysis of randomized trials evaluating antithrombotic strategies in patients with AF undergoing PCI, Cox proportional hazard models, stratified by trial, were used to estimate hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals (HR, 95%CI). The primary efficacy and safety outcomes were the composite of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke, and TIMI major bleeding, respectively. The study was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251130025). Six trials (10,634 patients) comparing DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor (4,083), VKA plus single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT, 1,247), VKA plus DAPT (3,715), and DOAC plus DAPT (1,589) were included. The transition from DAPT to SAPT was recommended at 1 (1-3) and 3 (1-7) days in the DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor and VKA plus SAPT groups, respectively. At 1 year, the risk of the primary efficacy outcome did not differ across the antithrombotic strategies (reference group: VKA plus DAPT; DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor: HR 1.16, 95%CI 0.97-1.41; VKA plus SAPT: 1.14, 0.85-1.54, DOAC plus DAPT: 0.99, 0.75-1.30), without any statistically significant interaction between treatment effects and all prespecified subgroups, including age, sex, bleeding risk, and thrombotic risk. However, 14-day landmark analysis showed an increased risk of myocardial infarction and definite/probable stent thrombosis in patients receiving DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor or VKA plus SAPT in the early phase after PCI. DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor reduced the risk of the primary safety outcome compared with VKA plus DAPT (0.48, 0.38- 0.65) and VKA plus SAPT (0.62, 0.40-0.97); only a borderline reduction was observed compared to DOAC plus DAPT (0.66, 0.44-1.01). DOAC plus P2Y12 inhibitor reduced intracranial hemorrhage compared with VKA plus DAPT (0.21, 0.07-0.64). In patients with AF undergoing PCI, the risk of cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, or stroke did not significantly differ according to whether patients received a DOAC or VKA, whereas a modest increase in risk with single compared with dual antiplatelet therapy cannot be excluded, given the higher risk of early coronary events. DOACs compared with VKAs reduced the risk of bleeding across all severity grades, including intracranial hemorrhage, whereas omission of a second antiplatelet agent reduced the risk of TIMI major or minor bleeding.

articles.title: Single Intranasal Administration of the Psychedelic Mebufotenin for Treatment-Resistant Depression: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: Psychedelics represent a potential breakthrough for treatment-resistant depression; however, the prolonged in-clinic monitoring required for compounds such as psilocybin and lysergic acid diethylamide is a logistical hurdle to widespread use. Intranasal mebufotenin (5-methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine), a 5-hydroxytryptamine 1A (5-HT1A) and 5-HT2A agonist associated with brief psychedelic experiences, may address this limitation. To evaluate the safety, efficacy, and time to discharge readiness following a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate in adults with treatment-resistant depression. Phase 2b, randomized, double-blind trial with an 8-week blinded follow-up conducted between September 2023 and April 2025 at 38 sites in Australia, Europe, and the US. Participants were aged 18 to 75 years with moderate to severe major depressive disorder nonresponsive to 2 to 5 antidepressant trials in the current episode. The last date of follow-up was April 28, 2025. After antidepressant washout as needed, participants were randomly assigned to receive a single dose of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate, 8 mg (n = 46), 12 mg (n = 73), or 0.3 mg (a low-dose comparator; n = 74), alongside psychological support. The primary end point was total score change on the Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS; score range, 0-60; higher scores indicate more severe depression) from baseline to day 29 in the 12-mg vs 0.3-mg dose groups. Eighteen secondary end points were assessed for the 12-mg and 8-mg vs 0.3-mg doses. Discharge readiness was assessed starting 90 minutes after dosing. Among the 193 included participants, the mean age was 41 (SD, 11.1) years and 59.1% were female. From baseline to day 29, treatment with 12-mg intranasal mebufotenin benzoate vs the 0.3-mg dose (the primary end point) was associated with significantly reduced MADRS scores (mean score change, -11.1 [SD, 11.6] vs -5.5 [SD, 9.9], respectively; mean difference, -5.3 [95% CI, -8.9 to -1.8]; P = .003). The 8-mg dose also led to reduced scores from baseline to day 29 (mean score change, -12.5 [SD, 12.7]) vs the 0.3-mg dose (mean difference, -6.2 [95% CI, -10.2 to -2.1]; P = .003). MADRS reductions with the 8-mg and 12-mg doses were similar and significantly greater at all other time points from 2 to 57 days post dose vs the 0.3-mg dose. Day 29 response rates were 35%, 34%, and 12% and remission rates were 26%, 18%, and 8% in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively. Treatment-emergent adverse events were reported in 76%, 85%, and 73% of participants in the 8-mg, 12-mg, and 0.3-mg dose groups, respectively; most events (99.7%) were mild or moderate. Overall, most participants were deemed ready for discharge within 2 hours post dose (85% for 8 mg and 78% for 12 mg). In adults with treatment-resistant depression, single doses of intranasal mebufotenin benzoate were well tolerated and produced rapid, robust, and durable reductions in depressive symptoms. Intranasal mebufotenin benzoate may improve treatment access and convenience, requiring a shorter monitoring period and fewer clinic visits compared with psilocybin and esketamine, respectively. articles.title: Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
articles.abstract: Retatrutide, an investigational triple agonist of glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide, glucagon-like peptide 1, and glucagon receptors, may be useful for treating obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). In two phase 3, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trials nested within larger basket trials of once-weekly subcutaneous retatrutide, we assigned adults with moderate-to-severe OSA and a body-mass index (the weight in kilograms divided by the square of the height in meters) of at least 27, without (TRIUMPH-1-OSA) or with (TRIUMPH-2-OSA) type 2 diabetes, to receive retatrutide (4, 9, or 12 mg) or placebo. The primary end point was the change in the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI, the average number of apneas and hypopneas per hour of sleep) at 80 weeks with 9 mg and 12 mg of retatrutide. For OSA-related end points, a hybrid-treatment estimand was applied, with a hypothetical strategy used for participants who had intercurrent events suggesting treatment failure and a treatment-policy strategy used elsewhere. We also report intention-to-treat (ITT) results. A total of 243 participants underwent randomization in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and 448 in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The baseline mean AHI was 58.6 and 55.9 events per hour, respectively, and the mean body weight was 119.6 and 115.9 kg. At 80 weeks, the mean changes in the AHI (hybrid-treatment estimand) with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-1-OSA were -22.9 (4 mg), -34.3 (9 mg), and -31.7 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -9.9 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -13.0 [95% confidence interval {CI}, -23.0 to -3.0], -24.4 [95% CI, -34.1 to -14.7], and -21.9 [95% CI, -32.2 to -11.5], respectively). The changes with retatrutide in TRIUMPH-2-OSA were -19.2 (4 mg), -24.7 (9 mg), and -25.4 (12 mg) events per hour, versus -10.3 with placebo (difference vs. placebo, -8.9 [95% CI, -15.9 to -2.0], -14.4 [95% CI, -21.6 to -7.2], and -15.1 [95% CI, -22.5 to -7.7]). For the ITT estimand, the corresponding differences from placebo were -13.2 (95% CI, -22.6 to -3.9), -24.7 (95% CI, -34.1 to -15.3), and -22.5 (95% CI, -31.9 to -13.1) in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -8.8 (95% CI, -15.8 to -1.7), -13.9 (95% CI, -21.3 to -6.6), and -15.0 (95% CI, -22.5 to -7.4) in TRIUMPH-2-OSA. The mean percent change in body weight with retatrutide (key secondary end point) was -12.5 to -22.2% in TRIUMPH-1-OSA and -12.1 to -18.5% in TRIUMPH-2-OSA, versus -4.8% and -5.6% with placebo (treatment-regimen estimand). The most common adverse events were gastrointestinal. In adults with OSA and obesity or overweight with or without type 2 diabetes, retatrutide resulted in significantly greater decreases in the AHI than placebo. Medical cannabis for the treatment of insomnia.
articles.abstract: Insomnia is highly prevalent and associated with substantial individual and societal burden, while existing pharmacological treatments are limited by adverse effects and concerns about long-term use. The role of medical cannabis in the treatment of insomnia remains unclear because of limited and heterogeneous evidence. Despite increasing clinical use, current guidelines do not provide clear recommendations due to uncertainty regarding its efficacy and safety. A clear synthesis of available evidence is needed to inform patients, clinicians, and policymakers about the potential benefits and harms of medical cannabis for insomnia. To assess the benefits and harms of medical cannabis in adults with insomnia. articles.title: Half-dose rivaroxaban vs antiplatelet therapy for preventing silent cerebral embolism after left atrial appendage occlusion: the HALO-SCE trial.
articles.abstract: The optimal long-term antithrombotic strategy after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) remains undetermined. The present study aimed to investigate whether half-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) could better reduce silent cerebral embolic lesions (SCEs) and preserve cognitive function compared to antiplatelet therapy after successful LAAO. In this investigator-initiated, prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial, patients with successful LAAO confirmed 45 days post-procedure were assigned 1:1 to half-dose rivaroxaban or antiplatelet therapy group. Diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging and cognitive assessments were repeated at 90, 180 and 365 days after LAAO. The primary outcome was the patient-level incidence of any newly detected SCE during follow-up. Secondary outcomes included cognitive trajectories, SCE burden, and a composite of all-cause mortality, clinical thromboembolic events and major bleeding. Between December 2022 and February 2025, 164 patients were randomized. The patient-level incidence of new SCEs was significantly lower in the half-dose rivaroxaban group than in the antiplatelet therapy group (10/82 [12.2%] vs. 26/82 [31.7%]; P = 0.005). The composite clinical outcome occurred in 2.4% of the half-dose rivaroxaban group vs. 11.0% of the antiplatelet therapy group (P = 0.057). In patients eligible for oral anticoagulation after successful LAAO, rivaroxaban 10 mg daily significantly reduced SCEs and better maintained cognitive function compared with antiplatelet therapy, with numerically fewer composite clinical events.

articles.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors Reduce Heart Failure Hospitalization, Cardiovascular Death and Kidney Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular disease and chronic kidney disease are the principal drivers of morbidity and mortality in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) have demonstrated cardiorenal benefits in landmark trials, yet cross-trial inconsistencies in cardiovascular mortality, renal endpoints and drug-specific effects leave the class-level estimates incompletely synthesized. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus and CENTRAL were searched from inception through 15 May 2026. Large placebo-controlled RCTs (≥ 1000 participants) and prespecified subgroup analyses in adults with T2DM were eligible. The primary outcome was the composite of first hospitalization for heart failure (HHF) or cardiovascular death (CV death). Secondary outcomes were 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), CV DEATH, myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, first HHF and composite kidney outcomes. Hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using random-effects inverse-variance models. Fourteen studies (76 969 patients; 41 761 SGLT2i, 35 208 placebo) were included. SGLT2i reduced the primary composite by 23% (HR: 0.77, 95% CI: 0.73-0.81, p < 0.0001; I = 0%), with no effect modification by baseline HF (p-interaction = 0.82) or established ASCVD (p-interaction = 0.46). MACE was reduced by 14% (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.81-0.92), driven by significant reductions in CV DEATH (HR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.79-0.93) and MI (HR: 0.88, 95% CI: 0.81-0.96), with no significant effect on stroke (HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.81-1.08). First, HHF was reduced by 29% (HR: 0.71, 95% CI: 0.66-0.77) and composite kidney outcomes by 31% (HR: 0.69, 95% CI: 0.60-0.79). SGLT2i confer consistent and clinically meaningful cardiorenal protection in T2DM across the full spectrum of cardiovascular and renal risk. The ertugliflozin estimate and the moderate heterogeneity in kidney outcomes should be interpreted in the context of trial-level clinical differences and nonstandardized kidney endpoint definitions. These findings support proactive, guideline-concordant initiation of evidence-based SGLT2i agents by endocrinologists, cardiologists and primary care providers as foundational therapy in T2DM.

articles.title: Petrelintide, a human amylin analogue for the treatment of obesity (ZUPREME 1): a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
articles.abstract: Petrelintide is a novel, long-acting amylin analogue being developed for long-term treatment of obesity, leveraging a mechanism of action distinct from incretin-based treatments. This phase 2 trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly petrelintide versus placebo in people with obesity. This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involved 32 sites (public hospitals and private clinics) in Poland, Romania, and the USA. Adults aged at least 18 years without type 2 diabetes, with a BMI of at least 30 kg/m or with a BMI of at least 27 kg/m with hypertension or dyslipidaemia, or both, were randomly assigned (5:1) to self-administered subcutaneous injections of once-weekly maintenance doses of petrelintide (1·0-9·0 mg) or placebo for 42 weeks including dose escalation. Randomisation was done via a central interactive response technology system and was stratified by MRI participation. Participants, trial staff, and the study funder were masked to treatment assignment but not to different maintenance doses; masking was maintained by use of identical vials for petrelintide and placebo. The primary endpoint was percentage change in bodyweight from baseline after 28 weeks. Analyses included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose. Missing data were assumed to be missing at random. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06662539) and the Clinical Trials Information System (2024-512549-18) and was completed on Mar 7, 2026. From Dec 9, 2024, to Feb 25, 2025, we screened 714 participants, of whom 493 were randomly assigned and 485 received at least one dose of petrelintide or placebo. 79 participants received at least one dose of treatment with petrelintide 1·0 mg, 81 with petrelintide 2·5 mg, 83 with petrelintide 5·0 mg, 79 with petrelintide 7·0 mg, 82 with petrelintide 9·0 mg, and 81 with placebo. 255 (53%) participants were female, 230 (47%) were male, mean age was 47 (SD 12) years, mean bodyweight 107·1 kg (20·3), mean BMI 36·7 kg/m (5·5), and 419 (86%) were White. Mean percentage change in bodyweight from baseline after 28 weeks (efficacy estimand) was -7·9% (95% CI -9·0 to -6·7) with petrelintide 1·0 mg, -7·9% (-9·0 to -6·7) with petrelintide 2·5 mg, -9·8% (-10·9 to -8·6) with petrelintide 5·0 mg, -9·3% (-10·5 to -8·2) with petrelintide 7·0 mg, and -9·4% (-10·5 to -8·3) with petrelintide 9·0 mg versus -1·7% (-2·8 to -0·5) with placebo. Estimated treatment differences versus placebo were -6·2% (-7·9 to -4·5) with petrelintide 1·0 mg, -6·2% (-7·8 to -4·5) with petrelintide 2·5 mg, -8·1% (-9·7 to -6·5) with petrelintide 5·0 mg, -7·7% (-9·3 to -6·0) with petrelintide 7·0 mg, and -7·7% (-9·4 to -6·1) with petrelintide 9·0 mg. Bodyweight continued to decline to week 42, with reductions of up to -10·7% with petrelintide. The most common adverse event with petrelintide was nausea (79 [20%] of 404 participants vs five [6%] participants with placebo). Vomiting was infrequent with petrelintide (12 [3%] participants vs five [6%] with placebo); active treatment and placebo had similarly low rates for diarrhoea (30 [7%] participants vs six [7%] with placebo) and constipation (28 [7%] vs three [4%] with placebo). No deaths were reported. Petrelintide achieved clinically meaningful weight reduction and had similar gastrointestinal tolerability to that of placebo apart from predominantly mild nausea during dose escalation, supporting further evaluation as a long-term obesity therapy. articles.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring in Non-Insulin-Treated Type 2 Diabetes.
articles.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) has been shown to be beneficial in persons with type 1 diabetes and others with insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, but its role in the treatment of persons with type 2 diabetes not being treated with insulin has needed further study. In a 26-week trial conducted at 22 primary care practices in the United States, we randomly assigned adults with type 2 diabetes who were not using insulin to either CGM or routine care (control). The primary outcome was the glycated hemoglobin level at 26 weeks. Key CGM-measured secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically to control the type I error rate. A total of 145 participants were assigned to the CGM group, and 138 to the routine-care group. Participants ranged in age from 21 to 84 years. The mean (±SD) glycated hemoglobin level decreased from 8.8±1.3% at baseline to 7.2±1.1% at 26 weeks in the CGM group and from 8.7±1.2% to 8.0±1.4% in the routine-care group (adjusted mean difference, -0.9 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -1.1 to -0.6; P<0.001). The mean percentage of time that the CGM-measured glucose level was in the glucose-level range of 70 to 180 mg per deciliter was 21 percentage points higher (95% CI, 16 to 26) with CGM than with routine care (P<0.001). The between-group difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 54 mg per deciliter was -0.17 percentage points (95% CI, -0.27 to -0.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority); the difference in the percentage of time that the glucose level was below 70 mg per deciliter was -0.20 percentage points (95% CI, -0.43 to -0.09; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P = 0.004 for superiority). No severe hypoglycemia events were reported. Among adults with type 2 diabetes that was not being treated with insulin and was being managed in a primary care setting, the use of CGM led to a greater reduction in the glycated hemoglobin level and to a lower risk of hyperglycemia than routine care. The primary end point was a viral load of less than 50 copies per milliliter at week 48; noninferiority was assessed with a margin of -10 percentage points. articles.abstract: OSA is associated with significant morbidity in pregnancy. Minimal guidance is available on how best to screen, diagnose, treat, and re-evaluate for OSA in pregnant patients. Considering the potentially adverse consequences of OSA in pregnancy if left untreated, we assembled a panel of experts to review the available literature methodologically and make evidence-based recommendations. Rigorous methodology was applied to provide a trustworthy evidence-based guideline and expert panel report. Panelists developed key clinical questions using the population, intervention, comparator, and outcome (PICO) format, addressing specific topics in OSA in pregnant individuals. MEDLINE (via PubMed) and the Cochrane Library were searched systematically for relevant literature and were supplemented by manual searches. References were screened with study evaluation tools to assess for inclusion, to extract meaningful data, and to grade the level of evidence to support each recommendation or suggestion. PICO questions related to screening, diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up of OSA in pregnant patients resulted in 9 conditional recommendations made with the evidence available and with the consensus of the expert panel. We recommend screening pregnant patients for OSA, either with a pregnancy-specific screening questionnaire or a standard tool. For those at risk of OSA based on screening, either a home sleep test or in-laboratory polysomnography is recommended for diagnosis. We recommend treatment for those with an apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) of 5 to 15 who have symptoms and sequelae or comorbidities, or those with an AHI of ≥ 15 regardless of symptoms or comorbidities, preferably with autotitrating positive airway pressure. Additionally, scheduled naps may be beneficial as an initial step in alleviating residual symptoms. Reassessment of OSA in the postpartum period is recommended in some patients. Because of the low level of certainty, 9 conditional recommendations were made for the screening, testing, and treatment of OSA in pregnancy.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonist Therapy for Glucocorticoid-Induced Dysglycaemia: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Glucocorticoids (GCs) commonly induce glycaemic disturbance, from transient steroid-induced hyperglycaemia to steroid-induced diabetes and contribute to post-transplant diabetes mellitus (PTDM). Insulin remains the standard treatment for GC-induced glycaemic dysregulation. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) have a mechanistic rationale here, but their efficacy and safety in GC-induced dysglycaemia have not been systematically appraised. A systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA 2020 guidelines (registration number: CRD420251183082). Embase, PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched up to May 2026. A structured narrative synthesis was the primary method. Thirteen studies were included, predominantly retrospective cohort studies; 10 enrolled solid organ transplant recipients with PTDM or pre-existing type 2 diabetes. GLP-1 RA therapy, either as monotherapy or as an adjunct to insulin, was associated with reductions in HbA1c and body weight, and a low rate of hypoglycaemia in the majority of included studies. GLP-1 RAs led to insulin dose reduction or discontinuation, reducing injection frequency and treatment burden. Five studies contributed to at least one pooled estimate, and no outcome was informed by more than three studies; given substantial heterogeneity and very low GRADE certainty, these estimates are exploratory and are presented in Supplementary Material 2. Individual studies reported reductions in HbA1c, body weight and insulin dose, with a low rate of hypoglycaemia episodes. However, available data specific to GC-induced dysglycaemia remain insufficient. Prospective controlled trials with explicit characterisation of GC exposure are required.

Diagnosis and Management of Adult Type 1 Diabetes Mellitus: Systematic Reviews of Biomarkers, Insulin Regimens and Insulin Delivery Devices Highlighting Evidence Gaps in Emergency and Humanitarian Settings.
articles.abstract: Supporting the World Health Organization's (WHO) 2021 Global Diabetes Compact's goals, we conducted three systematic reviews on type 1 diabetes (T1D) in adults concerning (1) diagnostic biomarkers, (2) insulin regimens and (3) insulin delivery devices, focusing on emergency and humanitarian settings. Multiple databases were searched in October 2024 without language or date restrictions. Two reviewers independently selected studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using study-specific tools. Critical outcomes included Haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c), hypoglycaemia, microvascular and macrovascular complications, diabetic ketoacidosis, mortality, adverse events, alongside diagnostic accuracy measures and patient-centred outcomes. Where appropriate, random-effects meta-analyses were performed, and certainty of evidence was assessed using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE). The biomarkers review (n = 15 studies) found C-peptide and other autoantibodies showed high specificity but variable sensitivity for T1DM diagnosis. The insulin regimen review (three reports from one small trial) suggested possible differences in glycaemic control and nephropathy outcomes between multiple daily and twice-daily regimens. The insulin delivery devices review (n = 8 studies) showed strong patient preference for pens; pooled analyses of HbA1c, hypoglycaemia and quality of life demonstrated outcomes comparable to syringes. Overall, the evidence was sparse, low quality and limited to high-income countries, with none of the studies addressing emergency or humanitarian settings. Certainty of evidence was very low for the biomarkers and delivery devices reviews and low for the insulin regimen review. Evidence for T1D care in emergency and humanitarian settings remains very limited. Evidence for biomarker use for diagnoses is constrained by very low-certainty evidence and infrastructure barriers. Multiple daily insulin regimens may confer glycaemic benefits, whereas pens and syringes yield similar outcomes despite patients' preference for pens. Evidence gaps underscore the need for pragmatic, context-sensitive guidance balancing clinical and logistical considerations. PROSPERO (CRD420250649000).

articles.title: Interventions for treatment of herpes labialis (cold sores on the lips).
articles.abstract: Herpes labialis (also known as cold sores or fever blisters) is a highly prevalent recurrent infection caused by the herpes simplex virus. Recurrences arise from varied triggers. Standard treatments usually involve nucleoside antivirals. Several studies have investigated alternative treatments such as zinc, honey, and photodynamic therapy for their potential to shorten lesion duration and relieve symptoms, but most reviews exclude these therapies. We wished to address this evidence gap by evaluating both conventional and alternative approaches, synthesising evidence on efficacy and safety to inform clinical practice and guide patient decisions. To assess the benefits and harms of interventions for treating herpes labialis in immunocompetent people. We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, and Embase on 23 September 2025, and we searched two clinical trial registries (ClinicalTrials.gov and World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform) on 1 October 2025. We included randomised controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling immunocompetent people with herpes labialis. Eligible interventions included topical, oral, and physical therapies (e.g. nucleoside antivirals, anti-inflammatory agents, phototherapy, photodynamic therapy). Eligible comparators were placebo, no treatment, or another active intervention. We applied no restrictions related to publication language or status (published, unpublished, in press, or in progress). Our critical outcomes were healing time (with healing defined as loss of crusts or all symptoms), rated by participants or investigators; and any adverse events leading to treatment cessation. Our important outcomes were participant-rated improvement of signs and symptoms (e.g. global rate of change scales), change from baseline in clinical episode severity (e.g. lesion size), change from baseline in pain severity, and any mild or moderate adverse events not leading to treatment cessation. We assessed the risk of bias using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool. We synthesised outcomes descriptively and pooled data with a random-effects meta-analysis using the inverse-variance method where appropriate. We reported dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RRs), continuous outcomes as mean differences (MDs), and time-to-event data as hazard ratios (HRs), all with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). For rare outcomes, we calculated the Peto odds ratio (OR). We assessed heterogeneity using the I² statistic and performed subgroup analyses by intervention or dose. We also conducted sensitivity analyses, excluding trials with high risk of bias. We rated the certainty of evidence using the GRADE approach. We included 87 RCTs with 22,631 participants. Forty-two trials were conducted in multiple centres and 39 in a single centre (the remaining 6 trials did not report number of centres). Most participants were adults (≥ 18 years), though some trials also enrolled younger individuals. The trials covered 58 interventions: 37 topical, eight oral, and 12 other therapies. Forty-three trials were industry funded, 25 received funding from non-profit organisations, one received no funding, and 18 did not report funding sources. No studies in our main comparisons reported participant-rated improvement of signs and symptoms, change from baseline in clinical episode severity, or change from baseline in pain severity. Topical aciclovir versus placebo Topical aciclovir probably reduces healing time compared with placebo (MD -0.88 days, 95% CI -1.43 to -0.33; I = 74%; 7 studies, 3475 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). The risk of adverse events leading to treatment cessation and the risk of mild or moderate adverse events are probably similar with topical aciclovir and placebo. Topical penciclovir versus placebo Topical penciclovir probably reduces healing time compared with placebo (MD -1.20 days, 95% CI -1.80 to -0.60; 528 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). The risk of adverse events leading to treatment cessation and the risk of mild or moderate adverse events are probably similar with topical penciclovir and placebo. Oral aciclovir versus placebo Oral aciclovir may result in little to no difference in healing time compared with placebo (MD -0.86 days, 95% CI -2.02 to 0.3; 1 study, 145 participants; low-certainty evidence). No studies in this comparison reported data for adverse effects. Oral valaciclovir versus placebo Oral valaciclovir reduces healing time compared with placebo (MD -1.05 days, 95% CI -1.40 to -0.70; P < 0.001, I² = 0%; 2 studies, 1218 participants). The trials evaluating this comparison reported no adverse events leading to treatment cessation. The risk of mild or moderate adverse events is probably similar with oral valaciclovir and placebo. Topical penciclovir versus topical aciclovir Topical penciclovir and topical aciclovir may have similar effects on healing time (hazard ratio (HR) 0.88, 95% CI 0.67 to 1.16; 1 study, 225 participants; low-certainty evidence). The trial evaluating this comparison reported no adverse events leading to treatment cessation. The risk of mild or moderate adverse events may be similar with topical penciclovir and topical aciclovir. Topical aciclovir versus oral aciclovir No trials compared topical aciclovir with oral aciclovir. Compared with placebo, topical nucleoside antivirals (aciclovir and penciclovir) probably reduce cold sore healing time by about one day. A study that compared topical penciclovir with topical aciclovir found that they may have similar effects on healing time. For oral nucleoside antivirals, we found that oral aciclovir compared with placebo may have little or no effect on healing time, while oral valaciclovir reduces healing time by about one day. The clinical importance of all reported reductions in healing time is uncertain, as no minimally important difference has been defined for this outcome in herpes labialis. Severe adverse events were rare, and mild or moderate adverse events were uncommon. Adverse events were generally balanced between treatments. From an equity standpoint, most studies focused on adults, predominantly women, with limited East Asian and paediatric representation. Future research should address these gaps by including under-represented groups and standardising outcomes for robust comparisons. Developing core outcome sets for recurrent herpes labialis would enhance consistency, support evidence synthesis, and guide clinicians towards more effective, equitable treatments globally. This review had no dedicated funding. Protocol (2022) DOI: 10.1002/14651858.CD015216.

articles.title: Association Between Kihon Checklist Oral-Function Score and All-Cause Mortality in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
articles.abstract: We examined whether the Kihon Checklist (KCL) oral-function score (0-3), based on three self-reported symptoms (chewing difficulty, dysphagia, and xerostomia), was associated with all-cause mortality in community-dwelling older adults. articles.title: DNL343 and Disease Progression in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract: DNL343 is a brain-penetrant small molecule that acts as an activator of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2B (eIF2b), designed to inhibit the integrated stress response. DNL343 was evaluated as a regimen of the HEALEY ALS Platform Trial, a double-blind, multiregimen, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial conducted at 74 centers in the US between May 24, 2023, and May 22, 2025. The analysis included shared randomized participants receiving placebo from an additional regimen. The study drug was administered for a placebo-controlled duration of 24 weeks. The primary analysis was a bayesian shared parameter model of function and survival that provided an integrated estimate of the relative rate of disease progression among participants receiving DNL343 relative to placebo. The model had components for function and survival linked through an integrated estimate of disease slowing in treatment relative to controls across the 2 outcomes (denoted as the disease rate ratio [DRR]). Several safety, secondary, and exploratory end points were also evaluated. A total of 259 screenings were completed in this regimen; 249 participants met eligibility and were randomized to DNL343 (n = 186) and regimen-specific placebo (n = 63), with an additional 76 participants from a concurrent regimen receiving placebo included for a total of 139 shared placebo participants (325 participants, with 196 (60.3%) male and mean [SD] age of 59.3 [11.5] years).
